📅 The 90-Day Plan

One quarter. Three goals. Measurable outcomes. Repeat four times a year.#

🏠 Home • 📋 Weekly tracker • 🗺️ Roadmaps

Why 90 days#

A year is too long to plan — you'll abandon it by February. A week is too short to achieve anything meaningful.

90 days is the sweet spot: long enough to genuinely learn a framework or ship a real project, short enough that you can hold the whole plan in your head and actually feel urgency.

Four of these a year. Sixteen across your degree. That's the whole game.

The rules#

  1. Maximum 3 goals. More than 3 means you achieve none of them.
  2. Every goal must be measurable. "Learn React" ❌ · "Build and deploy 2 React apps" ✅
  3. Write down the weekly commitment, not just the outcome.
  4. Review every Sunday using weekly-tracker.md.
  5. Don't change the goals mid-quarter. Adjust the plan, not the target.

Week 12 is a buffer week. Something will go wrong — exams, illness, a project that takes longer than planned. Plan for 11 weeks of work in 12 weeks of time.

🚧 What I'm saying NO to this quarter#

Every yes to something is a no to something else. Be explicit about it.

📚 Example plans

🌱 Year 1, Quarter 2 — Beginner

Goal 1 — DSA: Solve 80 problems (arrays, strings, hashing, basic recursion). Total: 20 → 100. Weekly: 7 problems, 5 hours

Goal 2 — Build: Learn HTML/CSS/JS fundamentals and build + deploy a personal portfolio plus 3 small vanilla-JS apps. Weekly: 6 hours

Goal 3 — Theory: Master OOP in my chosen language. Be able to explain all 4 pillars with my own examples. Weekly: 2 hours

Saying no to: learning React, joining a second college club, competitive programming.

🔨 Year 2, Quarter 3 — Building

Goal 1 — DSA: Solve 120 problems covering trees, graphs and basic DP. Total: 180 → 300. Weekly: 10 problems, 8 hours

Goal 2 — Build: Build and deploy a full-stack e-commerce app — JWT auth, PostgreSQL, Redis caching, Razorpay test payments, admin dashboard. Live URL + README with architecture diagram. Weekly: 10 hours

Goal 3 — Theory: DBMS complete + 50 SQL queries written by hand. Can explain normalisation, ACID and indexing out loud. Weekly: 3 hours

Saying no to: starting a second project, learning a new framework, hackathons this quarter.

🚀 Year 3, Quarter 1 — Getting hired

Goal 1 — DSA: Solve 100 problems (advanced graphs, DP patterns) + 12 LeetCode contests. Total: 300 → 400. Weekly: 8 problems + 1 contest, 8 hours

Goal 2 — Placement: Send 200 internship applications and 150 referral requests. Resume, LinkedIn and GitHub fully polished by week 2. Weekly: 18 applications, 13 referral requests, 4 hours

Goal 3 — Theory: OS + CN complete to interview level. 12 mock interviews done. Weekly: 3 hours + 1 mock

Saying no to: new projects, new technologies, anything that isn't directly hire-relevant.

⏰ Late start — 4th year, 8 months left

Goal 1 — DSA: Solve 180 problems (arrays, strings, hashing, two pointers, binary search, recursion, linked lists, stacks, trees). Total: 0 → 180. Weekly: 15 problems, 12 hours

Goal 2 — Build: One deployed full-stack app with auth and a database. Nothing fancy — finished and live. Weekly: 8 hours

Goal 3 — Placement: Aptitude prep complete (8-week plan) + apply to every service company and 100 off-campus roles. Weekly: 5 hours aptitude, 20 applications

Saying no to: learning anything new that isn't on this list, perfectionism on the project, waiting to feel ready.

→ roadmap/late-start.md

Three goals. Ninety days. Write it down, then go.#
